misleading_risk: Moderate, and mostly in the proposal's extras. (1) The visible line "No screenshot provided by the author" overclaims. The site only knows the manifest lists none. CellTracksColab's README has 8 screenshots, so the author did provide some, just not in the manifest. (2) A `shows` enum is an unverifiable author claim. A banner tagged `interface` passes, so it does not stop what it is meant to stop. (3) CellTracksColab's Wiki/Screenshot1.png and Screenshot2.png look like Google Colab notebook cells, with a "Show code" link and a Colab-style play button; I did not check how the desktop app renders the same notebook. Shown above the desktop "Get it" tiles, they could suggest the desktop app looks like Colab. The author's caption has to say what is shown, and the site must not add claims of its own. (4) NucleiSky 2D_QC.jpg shows SSIM=0.305 in the top-row error panel and SSIM=0.995 in the bottom row. Without an author caption explaining the two directions, a visitor may read 0.305 as the app's accuracy. The caption is the author's responsibility; the site should add no gloss. (5) Moving the figure above "Get it" pushes the OS download tiles below the fold. That conflicts with the benchmark's "one prominent download action" and with its Mac-install usability test. It is a visible trade-off, not a false statement.
refined_proposal:
Smaller version in three parts. The real P0 lever is content, because the site cannot invent pictures.

A. Content, done by the app owners in their own repos (author-controlled, no site code needed).
- NucleiSky: list docs/assets/2D_QC.jpg in labconstrictor-app.yaml. The author already uses it as "Example 2D QC overlay" in docs/qc.md:109. Replace the banner entry, because a title card is not a screenshot. The caption is the author's, for example what the eight panels show.
- CellTracksColab: list two or three of Wiki/Screenshot1.png (load data) and Screenshot2.png (track plot), plus Screenshot4.png if wanted. Use the README captions without the "Figure N:" prefix. Because they appear to be Colab notebook cells, the caption should say "in Google Colab" if that is true.
- The other four apps (GuessTheCondition, VLab4Mic, Playground, Demo) have no non-logo image in any git-tracked file, so the owners have to make one. The site cannot fix that.
- Until the manifests are merged, the dev-only seed/manifests/*.yaml carries these for previews.

B. Site code, one small commit.
1. In scripts/lcsite/pages_apps.py:203, emit alt=esc(caption). Move the loop into a small function such as shots_section(app). Remove "lc-shot__img" from DECORATIVE_IMAGE_PARENTS at scripts/check_design.py:22 so the code matches DESIGN.md:54 and the schema text "captions double as alt text". For a short caption, screen readers will read the text twice (alt and figcaption). I accept that over a rule that contradicts itself.
2. Add tests in tests/test_site.py. Render an app with a screenshot and check that the alt equals the escaped caption, that "<" in a caption is escaped, and that no figure appears when screenshots is []. Today nothing under tests/ renders a figure (only the fixture `screenshots: []` at test_site.py:11). Also add a case to the design-check test showing that an empty alt on lc-shot__img now fails.
3. Add one sentence to the schema description, DESIGN.md and content/submit.md, which has nothing on screenshots today (only line 32: "...DOI, screenshots and more"). For example: "A screenshot shows the app's window or a result it produced, with a caption that says what it shows; not a logo or banner." Authors read submit.md, so this costs no code and no schema property.
4. In catalogue.resolve, when the app is not section: testing and its manifest lists no screenshots, append one line to `warnings`: "{repo}: no screenshot listed; a screenshot of the window or of a result helps visitors decide". This reuses the existing mechanism. submit_app.py already prints app["warnings"] as "⚠" in the submission check, so new submitters see it. It also appears in build/problems.md under "Warnings (apps still listed)" and in the workflow step summary, and it opens no issue. Add a test for the warning and for its absence on a testing app. Keep it a warning, not an error: DESIGN/AGENTS allow optional manifest fields to be absent, and the benchmark's "required for a public listing" is a policy decision for the maintainers.

C. Do not build:
- the `shows` enum. It is unverifiable, it adds a schema property and a cross-repo sync of LabConstrictor_streamlit/schemas/labconstrictor-app.schema.json (which is an identical copy and is validated against in app_manifest.py), and it enforces nothing.
- the visible "No screenshot provided by the author" line. It overclaims, and it is developer-facing noise on visitor pages.
- the collapsed "More screenshots" details. The schema caps screenshots at 6, so a plain figure list is enough.
- the reference to a "Produces" section. No such section exists on the current app pages (the h2s are Get it, About, Using it, All downloads, How to install, Details), so the placement instruction cannot be followed as written.

Optional, and a design decision for the maintainers: show the first figure right after the header, before "Get it", as the benchmark orders it. If so, it must be loading="eager" (finish_site.py lazy-loads every image in main, and DESIGN.md says images above the fold do not lazy-load). It needs width and height attributes (none today, a CLS risk) and a CSS cap of about max-height 20rem. Measured on NucleiSky at 1280x800, the OS tiles now sit at y≈425–710; an uncapped figure of 1185x504 would push them to y≈950. Even capped they land at the fold. If the owners prefer the current order, leave the placement alone: the gain from simply swapping figure and About is only about 116 px (About h2 at y=1064, figure at y=1180).
